newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 16.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Wednesday.
- The Irish beef industry was rocked by a new BSE controversy on Tuesday after the unprecedented banning of three counties' produce from the 300-million-punt Russian market.
- Laws providing for the decommissioning of paramilitary arms will soon by introduced in the Irish and British parliaments following Tuesday's breakthrough in the multi-party talks at Stormont.
- The Irish government is to award a third mobile phone licence by the end of 1997 but industry experts said on Tuesday it is unlikely there will be heavy demand for the service.

- Banks, pension funds, insurance companies and other sources of private sector capital should be doing more to invest in infrastructural development which will underpin the future economic growth of Ireland, the director of the EU Cohesion Fund, Jean Francois Vertrynge said in Dublin on Tuesday.
- Four months after the multi-party talks began at Stomont delegates finally began addressing the vexed issue of the decommissioning of paramilitary weapons.

- There has been a general welcome for the sweeping powers granted to the tribunal of inquiry into the hepatitis C scandal, details of which were announced by the Minister for Health, Michael Noonan, on Tuesday.

- Plans to stage a production of West Side Story in front of a paying audience in Mountjoy Prison have received a mixed response from politicians and the Prison Officers' Association. The Irish government has responded to the critics by withdrawing tickets and promising a review of sales to date.
